docs.title: NDB-UFES Data Organizer
docs.text:
This repository organizes the public NDB-UFES / P-NDB-UFES oral histopathology data into leakage-safe cross-validation folds and supporting documentation.

The final product of this repo is not a trained model. It is a public data organization package: fold assignment files, data dictionary, factsheet, reproducibility notes, and audit guidance.

docs.title: Repository Purpose
docs.text:
• Create 6-fold assignments where all patches from the same origin image stay in the same fold, after Phase 2 morphology selection is accepted.
  • Document the dataset so external users can understand labels, demographics, risk factors, task fields, known limitations, and correct usage.
  • Use frozen pretrained embeddings only as an optional morphology-aware stratification signal.
  • Avoid downstream model-training claims or fold choices based on validation/test performance.

docs.title: Required Public Deliverables
docs.text: Deliverable Purpose fold_assignments_origin.csv One row per origin/WSI with fold, diagnosis, patch count, and morphology cluster where available. fold_assignments_patch_level*.csv Patch-level fold assignments with origin ID, diagnosis/class, fold, and image reference where available. Data Dictionary File relationships, columns, counts, labels, task fields, and missingness notes. Factsheet Dataset provenance, citation, task labels, demographics/risk factors, limitations, and leakage-safe use guidance. Exploratory Analysis Descriptive figures for diagnosis distributions, metadata, missingness, and association checks. Contamination Checks Image-level checks for suspicious patch similarity and origin-patch matching behavior. Reproducibility Commands, expected outputs, and audit checkpoints for regenerating artifacts. Pipeline Concise explanation of why each phase exists and how outputs flow. Implementation Status WIP status for each phase and notes about what still needs review.

docs.title: Manual Audit Guide
docs.text: Use this guide to manually verify generated code and artifacts before cleanup, publication, or commit.

docs.title: Audit Principle
docs.text: Trust artifacts only after checking data lineage and invariants. Generated prose, script comments, and filenames are not evidence by themselves.

docs.title: 1. Repo State and Ignored Files
docs.text:
Run:

git status --short
git status --ignored --short
git ls-files

Check:

  • Which files are tracked, modified, deleted, or untracked.
  • Whether data/ is intentionally DVC-managed and Git-ignored.
  • Whether results/ contains generated artifacts that should remain untracked.
  • Whether root Markdown files are temporary notes or canonical docs.
  • Whether accidental files exist, such as the empty file named 2.

Current known state:

  • many root Markdown files are untracked;
  • mkdocs.yml and docs/ are untracked;
  • scripts/phase3.py and scripts/phase4.py are empty;
  • main.py contains an obvious typo: neimport os.

docs.title: 2. Raw Data Lineage
docs.text:
Open:

  • data/ndb_ufes/patch/parcial_pndb_ufes.csv
  • data/ndb_ufes/origin_level/csvs/ndb-ufes.csv
  • data/ndb_ufes/patch_level/csvs/origin_patch_mapping.csv

Verify:

  • row counts match the data dictionary;
  • origin IDs are consistently typed and padded/unpadded intentionally;
  • patch image paths exist;
  • diagnosis values are limited to the expected three classes;
  • missing or Not informed values are documented.

Manual checks:

python3 - <<'PY'
import csv, collections
p = "data/ndb_ufes/patch/parcial_pndb_ufes.csv"
rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(p, newline="")))
print("rows", len(rows))
print("origins", len(set(r["origin"] for r in rows)))
print("diagnosis", collections.Counter(r["diagnosis"] for r in rows))
PY

docs.title: 3. Phase 1: Feature Extraction
docs.text:
Open in this order:

  1. scripts/phase1.py
  2. scripts/src/phase1/extraction_func.py
  3. scripts/src/phase1/feature_extractor.py
  4. scripts/src/models/model_loader.py
  5. scripts/src/models/model_wrappers.py
  6. scripts/src/phase1/config.yaml

What it should do:

  • create origin-patch mapping;
  • load frozen pretrained models;
  • extract patch embeddings;
  • save embeddings grouped by origin;
  • save run metadata.

Focal points:

  • path drift: patch/ versus patch_level/;
  • cache behavior: cached embeddings can hide changes;
  • preprocessing: ImageNet normalization is applied broadly, even for pathology foundation models;
  • wrapper behavior: models with different output shapes are forced through a common interface;
  • metadata wording: counts may refer to origins even when labeled as patches.

Evidence to collect:

  • number of origins in mapping;
  • total patch count across mapping;
  • one embedding file shape per model;
  • failed model list and failure reason.

docs.title: 4. Phase 2: Morphology Tuning
docs.text:
Open:

  • scripts/phase2.py
  • scripts/src/phase2/config.yaml
  • Phase 2 tuning outputs generated by the current rerun

What it should do:

  • discover Phase 1 embedding files;
  • mean-pool patch embeddings to one vector per origin;
  • run PCA and K-Means over a grid;
  • repeat K-Means runs;
  • save per-run, averaged, and selected-parameter outputs.

Focal points:

  • model-name parsing may collapse files such as efficientnet_b0 and efficientnet_b1 into one efficientnet key;
  • highest silhouette may prefer too few clusters for useful fold stratification;
  • existing folds may reflect an older morphology-clustering configuration;
  • selection must not depend on downstream model performance.

Audit questions:

  • Are all intended embedding files discovered?
  • Are any discovered models overwritten by filename parsing?
  • Are cluster sizes reasonable?
  • Is the chosen model/config justified for fold stratification, not just mathematical cluster separation?
  • Are repeated runs summarized with mean and standard deviation?

docs.title: 5. Leakage Review
docs.text:
Acceptable:

  • frozen external pretrained embeddings used for unsupervised fold stratification;
  • choosing folds before downstream model training.

Leakage or selection-bias risks:

  • patch-level random splitting;
  • selecting folds after downstream test results;
  • fine-tuning embeddings on all labels before fold creation;
  • using the same origin in train and test through different patches.

Required invariant:

one origin_id -> one fold

docs.title: 6. Phase 3: Fold Creation
docs.text:
Open:

  • scripts/phase3.py
  • scripts/src/phase3/phase3_fold_creation.py
  • scripts/src/phase3/phase3_fold_visualization.py
  • existing fold CSVs under data/ndb_ufes/*/csvs/

What it should do:

  • load origin/patch metadata;
  • apply chosen PCA/K-Means clustering;
  • assign morphology clusters;
  • create stratification variables;
  • assign origins to folds;
  • broadcast fold assignments to patch rows.

Focal points:

  • top-level scripts/phase3.py is empty;
  • implementation file may write to results/phase3_fold_creation/, while current artifacts are under data/ndb_ufes/;
  • existing folds may rely on an older morphology-clustering configuration;
  • default fold-construction variables should be origin diagnosis, morphology cluster, gender, and age group;
  • inspect stratification_variables_audit.csv before accepting any rerun;
  • high-missingness fields such as Not informed-heavy clinical variables must not silently enter stratification_key;
  • some docs describe old fold-column formats that no longer match current CSVs.

Manual invariant check:

python3 - <<'PY'
import csv, collections
rows = list(csv.DictReader(open("data/ndb_ufes/patch_level/csvs/fold_assignments_patch_level_detailed.csv", newline="")))
by_origin = collections.defaultdict(set)
for r in rows:
    by_origin[r["origin_id"]].add(r["fold"])
print("bad origins", sum(len(v) != 1 for v in by_origin.values()))
print("patch fold counts", collections.Counter(r["fold"] for r in rows))
PY

Missingness-aware stratification audit:

python3 - <<'PY'
import csv
p = "results/phase3_fold_creation/stratification_variables_audit.csv"
rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(p, newline="")))
for r in rows:
    print(r["column"], r["status"], r["missing_rate"], r["reason"])
PY

Expected policy:

  • origin_diagnosis, morph_cluster, gender, and age_group are included by default.
  • additional demographic and clinical fields remain descriptive unless explicitly promoted and accepted by the audit gate.
  • variables with high Not informed or missing rates are excluded from fold construction.

docs.title: 7. Phase 4: Validation
docs.text:
Open:

  • scripts/phase4.py
  • scripts/src/phase4/phase4_feature_analysis.py
  • scripts/src/phase4/phase4_data_analysis.py
  • scripts/src/phase4/phase4_causal_interpretability.py

What it should do:

  • validate fold balance and origin integrity;
  • summarize distributions;
  • optionally extend fold files with metadata useful for factsheets and subgroup reporting.

Focal points:

  • top-level scripts/phase4.py is empty;
  • some paths are stale;
  • chi-square p-values should not be interpreted as proof of balance;
  • causal/interpretable metadata should be documented descriptively unless a separate causal design exists.

docs.title: 8. Factsheet and Data Dictionary Completeness
docs.text:
Check:

  • provenance and citation are present;
  • diagnosis labels and task labels are defined;
  • demographic/risk-factor fields are listed;
  • missingness and Not informed values are visible;
  • limitations are explicit;
  • leakage-safe use guidance is prominent;
  • fold files and schemas match actual CSVs.

docs.title: 9. Documentation Cleanup
docs.text:
After audit, decide for each root Markdown file:

  • promote content into docs/;
  • archive as historical notes;
  • delete if superseded.

Do not commit both root duplicates and docs pages unless each has a distinct purpose.

docs.title: Final Acceptance Checklist
docs.text:
• Every public command in README/docs points to an existing script.
  • Empty entrypoints are implemented, removed, or clearly documented.
  • Fold assignment files pass origin-integrity checks.
  • Phase 2 model/config choice is documented and not chosen from downstream performance.
  • Factsheet is mandatory and complete.
  • Data dictionary reflects actual current CSV schemas.
  • Root scratch Markdown files are cleaned up only after manual review.

docs.title: Contamination Checks
docs.text: This page records image-level checks used to inspect possible contamination, duplicate-like patches, and origin-patch matching behavior. These checks are exploratory quality-control material and should be reviewed before final fold publication.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The contamination checks are intended to answer practical data-organization questions:

  • whether visually similar patches are duplicates or near-duplicates;
  • whether patches can be traced back to the expected origin image;
  • whether suspicious examples require exclusion, relabeling, or documentation;
  • whether fold construction needs extra safeguards beyond origin-level grouping.

docs.title: Task Labels
docs.text:
The source study defines four classification tasks across RMDS and NDB-UFES. This repository organizes NDB-UFES, so Task II, Task III, and Task IV are the relevant task fields.

Task Dataset Labels Definition Task I RMDS Normal / OSCC Histopathological-image classification for normal versus OSCC samples. No demographic or clinical data are available. Not part of this NDB-UFES organizer. Task II NDB-UFES Leukoplakia / OSCC Differentiates samples diagnosed as leukoplakia or OSCC. Task III NDB-UFES Absence / Presence of dysplasia Differentiates samples identified with or without dysplasia. OSCC lesions are labeled as presence of dysplasia. Task IV NDB-UFES OSCC / Leukoplakia with dysplasia / Leukoplakia without dysplasia Three-class diagnosis task.

Observed task label values in the current patch metadata:

Field Observed values Interpretation for users TaskII OSCC, Leukoplakia Binary OSCC vs leukoplakia grouping. TaskIII Presence, Absence Dysplasia presence grouping; OSCC is included in Presence. TaskIV OSCC, Leukoplakia with dysplasia, Leukoplakia without dysplasia Three-class diagnostic task.

The source paper reports the full origin-level NDB-UFES task counts as: Task II: 146 leukoplakia and 91 OSCC; Task III: 180 presence and 57 absence; Task IV: 91 OSCC, 89 leukoplakia with dysplasia, and 57 leukoplakia without dysplasia.

docs.title: Exploratory Analysis
docs.text: This page collects exploratory dataset figures generated during the dataset organization work. These plots are descriptive: they document the available metadata, matched subset, missingness, and variable relationships used to decide what should be included in the public factsheet and what should not silently drive fold construction.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
The exploratory analysis currently covers:

  • diagnosis distributions at origin and patch level;
  • task label availability for Tasks II, III, and IV;
  • demographic and clinical metadata distributions;
  • missing and Not informed rates;
  • diagnosis cross-tabs against available clinical variables;
  • categorical association summaries.

The figures are used as audit material for documentation and fold-design decisions. They are not downstream model performance results.

docs.title: Diagnosis Matching
docs.text: The matched subset links patch-level records back to origin-level metadata. Diagnosis matching is checked before fold design because folds must be assigned at origin level and then inherited by patches.

docs.title: Demographic and Clinical Metadata
docs.text: The available metadata includes demographic fields and clinical risk-factor fields. These variables are documented in the public dataset factsheet, but they are not automatically suitable as fold-construction strata.

docs.title: Missingness
docs.text: Missing and Not informed rates are checked separately at origin and patch level. Variables with high missingness should be treated carefully and usually remain descriptive unless explicitly promoted after review.

docs.title: Association Checks
docs.text: Categorical association plots help identify relationships worth documenting and checking during fold review. These summaries should not be interpreted as causal evidence.

docs.title: Dataset Factsheet
docs.text: This factsheet summarizes the organized NDB-UFES data package produced by this repository. It is intended for public dataset users who need to understand provenance, labels, folds, demographics/risk factors, limitations, and leakage-safe usage.

  • patch-level fold assignments,
  • data dictionary,

docs.title: Demographics and Risk Factors
docs.text:
The organized patch metadata includes:

  • gender
  • skin_color
  • age_group (0: younger than 40 years, 1: 40-60 years, 2: older than 60 years)
  • tobacco_use
  • alcohol_consumption
  • sun_exposure
  • localization
  • larger_size
  • dysplasia_severity
  • ROI coordinates: top_left_x, top_left_y, bottom_right_x, bottom_right_y (deferred; these need to be rerun because some previous patch-origin associations were incorrect)

Observed missingness is substantial for some fields. For example, patch-level Not informed values appear in skin color, tobacco use, alcohol consumption, and sun exposure. These fields are useful for documentation and subgroup reporting, but should not be treated as complete clinical covariates without checking missingness.

docs.title: Fold Construction Status
docs.text:
Fold construction is not treated as final while the project is still auditing Phase 2 morphology selection. The intended fold design is:

  • all patches from the same origin stay in the same fold;
  • folds are balanced by patch count;
  • folds preserve diagnostic class distribution;
  • morphology-aware clustering can be used as an additional stratification signal.

There are existing fold CSV artifacts in the worktree from a previous run, but they should be treated as provisional audit material until Phase 2 model/config selection is accepted or folds are regenerated.

docs.title: Leakage-Safe Usage
docs.text:
Required:

  • split by fold, not by random patch rows;
  • keep all rows with the same origin_id in the same train/validation/test partition;
  • once finalized, use the provided fold assignments when comparing models;
  • document which fold(s) were used for train, validation, and test.

Avoid:

  • random patch-level splits;
  • selecting folds after seeing downstream model performance;
  • fine-tuning an embedding model on all labels before using its features to construct folds;
  • treating patches from the same origin as independent observations in evaluation.

Frozen external pretrained embeddings used only for unsupervised morphology-aware stratification are acceptable as a data organization step, provided downstream model performance did not influence the stratification choice.

• The repo is mid-reorganization; some generated root Markdown files are not canonical.
  • scripts/phase3.py and scripts/phase4.py are currently empty top-level entrypoints.
  • Phase 2 morphology tuning will be rerun before final fold publication; provisional fold artifacts should not be treated as final until they are checked against the accepted configuration.

docs.text:

docs.title: For Phase 2 (Clustering)
docs.text:
import pickle
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load embeddings
with open('data/embeddings/embeddings_wsi_level_uni_20260421_183206.pkl', 'rb') as f:
    patch_features = pickle.load(f)

# Convert to WSI-level (mean pool)
wsi_features = {
    origin_id: features.mean(axis=0)
    for origin_id, features in patch_features.items()
}

# Stack into matrix for clustering
X = np.array([wsi_features[oid] for oid in sorted(wsi_features.keys())])  # (203, 768)

# Apply PCA + K-Means (Phase 2)
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans

pca = PCA(n_components=15)
X_pca = pca.fit_transform(X)  # (203, 15)

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=4)
clusters = kmeans.fit_predict(X_pca)  # (203,)

docs.title: Pipeline Overview
docs.text: The pipeline organizes a public oral histopathology dataset into leakage-safe folds. Its purpose is data organization and documentation, not downstream model training.

  -> Phase 3: leakage-safe fold creation

docs.title: Phase 1: Feature Extraction
docs.text:
Goal: create origin-patch mappings and frozen embedding files that can be used for morphology-aware fold stratification.

Current entrypoint:

uv run python scripts/phase1.py

Main implementation files:

  • scripts/phase1.py
  • scripts/src/phase1/extraction_func.py
  • scripts/src/phase1/feature_extractor.py
  • scripts/src/models/model_loader.py
  • scripts/src/models/model_wrappers.py
  • scripts/src/phase1/config.yaml

Expected inputs:

  • data/ndb_ufes/patch/parcial_pndb_ufes.csv
  • patch images under data/ndb_ufes/patch_level/images/ or data/ndb_ufes/patch/images/, depending on the script path being audited

Expected outputs:

  • data/ndb_ufes/patch_level/csvs/origin_patch_mapping.csv
  • data/embeddings/embeddings_wsi_level_{model}_{timestamp}.pkl
  • results/phase1_metadata/
  • optional feature cache under results/phase1_feature_cache/

Audit focus:

  • Confirm all patch paths exist and point to the intended image directory.
  • Confirm output embeddings are grouped by origin and contain patch-level vectors.
  • Confirm caches are not stale before accepting regenerated outputs.
  • Confirm model wrappers and preprocessing are appropriate for each model family.

docs.title: Phase 2: Morphology Tuning
docs.text:
Goal: identify frozen embedding models and PCA/K-Means settings that produce useful morphology strata for fold balancing.

Current entrypoint:

uv run python scripts/phase2.py

Main implementation files:

  • scripts/phase2.py
  • scripts/src/phase2/config.yaml

Current configuration:

  • PCA components: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 15, 18, 20, 25, 30
  • K-Means clusters: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9
  • repeated runs: 5
  • primary metric in code: silhouette

Expected inputs:

  • data/embeddings/embeddings_wsi_level_*.pkl
  • data/ndb_ufes/origin_level/csvs/ndb-ufes.csv

Expected outputs when rerun:

  • per-model tuning tables;
  • averaged tuning summaries;
  • selected-parameter files;
  • visual summaries for reviewing PCA/K-Means behavior.

These files are not treated as committed documentation artifacts yet because Phase 2 will be rerun before final fold creation.

Audit focus:

  • Repeated K-Means should use mean and standard deviation across runs.
  • Five runs is the recommended default; three runs is only an exploratory shortcut.
  • Do not select the model/config using downstream training or test results.
  • Do not rely only on highest silhouette. Also check cluster sizes, stability, interpretability, and whether clusters are useful for fold stratification.
  • Existing provisional folds should be checked against the final accepted Phase 2 configuration before publication.

docs.title: Phase 3: Fold Creation
docs.text:
Goal: assign every origin to exactly one fold, then broadcast that assignment to every patch.

Current state:

  • scripts/phase3.py is empty.
  • Implementation exists at scripts/src/phase3/phase3_fold_creation.py.
  • Existing provisional fold outputs are currently under data/ndb_ufes/origin_level/csvs/ and data/ndb_ufes/patch_level/csvs/.

  • data/ndb_ufes/origin_level/csvs/fold_assignments_origin.csv
  • data/ndb_ufes/patch_level/csvs/fold_assignments_patch_level.csv
  • data/ndb_ufes/patch_level/csvs/fold_assignments_patch_level_detailed.csv
  • data/ndb_ufes/patch_level/csvs/fold_assignments_patch_level_with_images.csv

Audit focus:

  • Every patch has exactly one origin.
  • Every origin appears in exactly one fold.
  • Every patch inherits its origin's fold.
  • Fold balance is checked by patch count, origin count, diagnosis, morphology cluster, gender, and age group.
  • Fold construction should use origin diagnosis, the selected morphology cluster, gender, and age group by default.
  • Other demographic and clinical fields with high Not informed/missingness are factsheet descriptors, not automatic stratification variables.
  • Any additional demographic or clinical field promoted into fold construction must pass the saved stratification-variable audit.
  • Provisional folds must be compared with the final accepted Phase 2 morphology configuration before treating them as final.

docs.title: Leakage Policy
docs.text:
Acceptable:

  • Frozen external pretrained embeddings used for unsupervised morphology-aware stratification.
  • Selecting fold strata before downstream model training.

Not acceptable:

  • Fine-tuning the embedding model on all dataset labels before fold creation.
  • Choosing folds or the stratification model because they improve downstream validation/test performance.
  • Splitting patches from the same origin across train/validation/test folds.

docs.title: Phase 2: Morphology Tuning
docs.text:
Command:

uv run python scripts/phase2.py

Expected outputs when rerun:

  • per-model tuning tables;
  • averaged tuning summaries;
  • selected-parameter files;
  • visual summaries for reviewing PCA/K-Means behavior.

These files are not treated as fixed documentation artifacts yet because Phase 2 is expected to be rerun.

Recommended policy:

  • use 5 repeated K-Means runs by default;
  • use 3 only as an exploratory shortcut;
  • compare mean and standard deviation, cluster sizes, and interpretability;
  • do not select the stratification configuration using downstream model performance.

After rerun, summarize candidate configurations only after confirming the output schema and accepted model list.

docs.title: Phase 3: Fold Creation
docs.text:
Do not treat the top-level scripts/phase3.py as working until it is implemented.

Implementation file to audit:

scripts/src/phase3/phase3_fold_creation.py

Existing fold outputs to audit:

  • data/ndb_ufes/origin_level/csvs/fold_assignments_origin.csv
  • data/ndb_ufes/patch_level/csvs/fold_assignments_patch_level.csv
  • data/ndb_ufes/patch_level/csvs/fold_assignments_patch_level_detailed.csv
  • data/ndb_ufes/patch_level/csvs/fold_assignments_patch_level_with_images.csv

Expected output from a current Phase 3 rerun:

  • results/phase3_fold_creation/stratification_variables_audit.csv

The audit file records which variables entered the fold key and why additional demographic/clinical variables were excluded or retained as descriptive fields.

Invariant check:

uv run python - <<'PY'
import csv, collections
patch_file = "data/ndb_ufes/patch_level/csvs/fold_assignments_patch_level_detailed.csv"
rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(patch_file, newline="")))
by_origin = collections.defaultdict(set)
fold_counts = collections.Counter()
for r in rows:
    by_origin[r["origin_id"]].add(r["fold"])
    fold_counts[r["fold"]] += 1
bad = {origin: folds for origin, folds in by_origin.items() if len(folds) != 1}
print("patch rows:", len(rows))
print("origins:", len(by_origin))
print("fold counts:", dict(sorted(fold_counts.items())))
print("origins spanning multiple folds:", len(bad))
PY

Observed provisional artifact shape:

  • 3,086 patch rows;
  • 203 origins;
  • zero origins spanning multiple folds.

Do not treat fold counts as final while Phase 2 morphology selection remains under audit. A current Phase 3 rerun should also produce stratification_variables_audit.csv, showing which variables were included in or excluded from fold construction.

docs.title: Setup & Installation
docs.text: Complete step-by-step guide to setting up the NDB-UFES Data Organizer on your local machine.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
• Python: 3.10-3.12 (3.12 recommended)
  • OS: macOS (M1/M2/M3/M4), Linux, or Windows
  • Storage: ~20 GB for full dataset (DVC S3 remote)
  • GPU/Accelerator:
  • Optional: NVIDIA CUDA 11.8+ (Linux)
  • Optional: Apple Metal Performance (macOS M-series)
  • CPU mode supported but slower

docs.title: Step 1: Clone Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/yourusername/ndb_ufes_data_organizer.git
cd ndb_ufes_data_organizer

docs.title: Step 2: Install uv
docs.text:
Install uv if it is not already available:

curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
uv --version

uv creates and manages the project virtual environment in .venv/.

docs.title: Step 3: Install Dependencies
docs.text:
uv sync

Key packages (see pyproject.toml for full list): - torch>=2.0.0 — Deep learning framework - torchvision>=0.15.0 — Vision utilities - transformers>=4.30.0 — HuggingFace model hub - scikit-learn>=1.6.1 — Clustering + preprocessing - pandas>=2.2.3 — Data manipulation - numpy>=2.2.1 — Numerical computing - plotly>=5.13.0 — Interactive 3D visualizations - dvc>=3.58.0 — Data version control - dvc-s3>=3.2.0 — AWS S3 remote for DVC - timm==1.0.26 — PyTorch Image Models

Installation time: 5-10 minutes (depending on internet speed)

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
uv run python -c "import torch; print(f'PyTorch version: {torch.__version__}')"
uv run python -c "import transformers; print(f'Transformers version: {transformers.__version__}')"

docs.title: Download Data
docs.text:
The dataset is version-controlled with DVC (Data Version Control) on AWS S3.

# Initialize DVC (if not already done)
uv run dvc remote list  # Should show 's3://dvc-ndb-ufes/data' as default

# Download all data (images, CSVs, metadata)
uv run dvc pull

Expected download: - data/ndb_ufes/origin_level/ — 238 WSI images (~5 GB) - data/ndb_ufes/patch_level/images/ — 3,768 patch images (~2 GB) - data/ndb_ufes/patch_level/csvs/ — Metadata CSVs (~1 MB) - data/ndb_ufes/link_level/ — 3,055 link images (~2 GB)

Download time: 10-20 minutes (depending on network)

docs.title: DVC Configuration
docs.text:
DVC remote is pre-configured in data.dvc: 

remote:
  s3:
    url: s3://dvc-ndb-ufes/data

To use custom AWS credentials, set environment variables: 

export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=your_key
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=your_secret

docs.title: Step 5: Setup API Credentials (Optional but Recommended)
HuggingFace Hub
docs.text:
Several models require authentication for optimal performance:

# Interactive login
uv run huggingface-cli login

# Or via environment variable
export HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=your_token_here

Get your token from huggingface.co/settings/tokens.

To view this documentation site locally with embedded visualizations:

docs.title: Issue: torch import fails
docs.text:
Solution: Reinstall PyTorch for your device: 

# For Apple Silicon (M-series)
uv pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/cpu

# For NVIDIA CUDA 11.8
uv pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu118

docs.title: Issue: DVC pull fails with S3 error
docs.text:
Solution: Check AWS credentials and DVC config: 

aws sts get-caller-identity  # Verify AWS credentials
uv run dvc remote list  # Check remote configuration
uv run dvc pull -vv  # Verbose output for debugging

docs.title: Issue: HuggingFace model download is slow/fails
docs.text:
Solution: Set HF cache directory and retry: 

export HF_HOME=/path/to/cache  # Use faster disk if available
uv run python scripts/phase1.py  # Retry with cache

docs.title: Issue: Out of memory (OOM) during extraction
docs.text:
Solution: Reduce batch size in scripts/phase1.py: 

BATCH_SIZE = 32  # Change to 16 or 8

docs.title: Issue: GPU/MPS not detected
docs.text:
Solution: Check device setup: 

# For MPS (Apple Metal)
import torch
print(torch.backends.mps.is_available())  # Should be True
print(torch.backends.mps.is_built())       # Should be True

# For CUDA
torch.cuda.is_available()  # Should be True
torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)  # Should show GPU name

docs.title: Implementation Status
docs.text: This page records what each phase is intended to do and what still needs review. The repository is mid-reorganization, so this page is intentionally conservative.

docs.title: Phase 0: Data Checks and Contamination Review
docs.text:
Purpose:

  • inspect image matching between patches and origin images;
  • identify duplicate-like or suspicious patch cases;
  • document any exclusions or accepted limitations.

WIP - current:

  • this stage is being used for manual data-quality review.

WIP - planned:

  • consolidate accepted, excluded, and documented suspicious cases;
  • reflect any decisions in the data dictionary and reproducibility notes.

Status: WIP.

docs.title: Phase 1: Feature Extraction
docs.text:
Purpose:

  • create origin-patch mapping;
  • extract frozen embeddings for candidate pretrained models;
  • save WSI-level embedding dictionaries for Phase 2.

WIP - current:

  • active entrypoint: scripts/phase1.py;
  • implementation files are under scripts/src/phase1/ and scripts/src/models/;
  • run metadata is written under results/phase1_metadata/.

WIP - planned:

  • rerun after final path checks;
  • confirm generated embeddings are grouped correctly by origin;
  • keep embedding visualizations as exploratory review material, not as Phase 1 acceptance criteria.

Status: implemented, still needs final rerun/audit before publication.

docs.title: Phase 2: Morphology Tuning
docs.text:
Purpose:

  • aggregate patch embeddings to origin-level vectors;
  • evaluate PCA/K-Means combinations;
  • generate tuning plots and parameter files;
  • select a morphology signal for fold stratification.

WIP - current:

  • active entrypoint: scripts/phase2.py;
  • code exists for repeated PCA/K-Means tuning across embedding models;
  • outputs are intentionally not documented as committed results because this phase will be rerun.

WIP - planned:

  • rerun Phase 2 after accepting Phase 1 embeddings;
  • review cluster sizes, stability, silhouette, and interpretability;
  • select one morphology configuration for Phase 3.

Status: implemented, selection WIP.

docs.title: Phase 3: Fold Creation
docs.text:
Purpose:

  • assign each origin to one fold;
  • broadcast origin folds to patch-level records;
  • balance folds by diagnosis and accepted stratification variables;
  • save public fold assignment CSVs.

WIP - current:

  • top-level scripts/phase3.py is not yet an active entrypoint;
  • implementation code exists under scripts/src/phase3/;
  • some helper visualization scripts are exploratory and should be reviewed before committing as final pipeline code;
  • provisional fold artifacts exist, but should be compared against the accepted Phase 2 configuration.

WIP - planned:

  • wire a clean Phase 3 entrypoint;
  • generate final origin-level and patch-level fold CSVs;
  • verify origin integrity, patch inheritance, and fold balance;
  • decide which visualization helpers survive as part of the final phase.

Status: WIP.

docs.text:

  • validate fold invariants;
  • summarize dataset distributions and limitations;
  • prepare final data dictionary, factsheet, and reproducibility notes.

WIP - current:

  • top-level scripts/phase4.py is not yet an active entrypoint;
